topics.topic: Ownership, recording, and verification of dependency and sandbox-runtime version pins
questions: What module or named build component owns selecting, recording and verifying the exact dependency and sandbox-runtime versions required by A20?
Does `data_provider` own the exact dependency and sandbox-runtime pins, or does an unnamed release/build component own and verify them?

quotes: Each accepted decision has one primary owner, the module that holds the decision's central mechanism, and consumers. Ownership is by rule, not by decision: a consumer owns exactly the rules and parts of the decision its own section below names, and the primary owner owns every rule of the decision that no other section names.

A20: the release constants generated code reads — one `RELEASE_CEILING_<NAME>` per ceiling with the values of release v1; the closed lists of trapped standard-library entry points of A03 rule 4 and the sandbox environment of A03 rule 1; the minimum token length of A16 rule 1; the instance classes that allow plain `http` and the class an absent or unknown one counts as (A09 rule 4); the headers the kernel sets itself and the one of them an instance may set instead (A08 rule 5); the form of a `service_id` and the file name suffix of a service record (A08 rule 1).

The pinned Python dependencies and sandbox runtime of A20 rule 3 are a release artifact built and checked outside the running kernel; at run time only `sandbox.probe_sandbox` checks that a sandbox works.

A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython 3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list. A vulnerable dependency is answered by a new release; a running kernel never updates one.

The kernel imports only the standard library of CPython 3.12; no third-party package (`imports.third_party` is empty by this decision). The entrance is `http.server.HTTPServer`, which serves one request at a time (A18 rule 3); services are called through `http.client`, which lets the kernel send exactly the headers of A10; the store is `sqlite3`. Two host programs belong to the release with the interpreter: `git`, through which `bindings` reads a manifest record as a git object (decision 8), and `bwrap` (A03). The release names their versions; the kernel runs no other program.
judgement.divergence: One implementer makes `data_provider`, as A20's primary owner, select and expose the exact interpreter, dependency, `git`, and `bwrap` pins and their verification; another leaves selection, recording, and verification entirely to an unnamed release/build pipeline while `data_provider` contains only runtime constants. Release maintainers and the owner notice different release artifacts and different guarantees that the required versions were verified.
judgement.why: The texts require exact release pins and assign A20 a primary module owner, but they neither state whether dependency pins are owned by `data_provider` nor name the external build component that would own and verify them.

topics.topic: Ownership and declaration location of the StoreRepository interface
questions: Which module owns and declares the `StoreRepository` interface itself, so its implementation does not violate the rule that `store_persistence` may know only `models`?

topics.topic: Ownership and propagation of the credential-read text-size ceiling
questions: Which module owns applying `bounded_text_bytes_max` while the credential file is read, and how may it obtain that ceiling?

topics.topic: Ownership of attempt-number assignment for pre-execution spooled files
questions: Who computes and supplies the attempt number to `store.spool_file` for a file written before its concluding NodeExecution?

topics.topic: Persistence-layer exemption from higher-module record ownership rules
questions: Are `store` and `store_persistence` exempt from the rule against reading records owned by higher modules for persistence-only operations?

topics.topic: SQLite operation boundary between store and store_persistence
questions: Which module is permitted to invoke SQLite operations, and what exactly does “touches the database” exclude?

topics.topic: Whether canonical_values receives or retrieves applicable size bounds
questions: Does `canonical_values.fit_port_value` read release ceilings itself, or must each calling module choose and pass the applicable size bound?
